---
title: "Administrative recognition of autism in Chile, 2019–2025"
subtitle: "A multisource study of the routine records of the public health and education systems"
---

```{python}
#| label: cargar-resumen
from pathlib import Path
import json
import sys
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path.cwd().parent if Path.cwd().name == "docs" else Path.cwd()
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "docs" / "study"))
from report_helpers import read_result, kpis, number, share, show_table, ci

grd_sources = read_result("grd_source_inventory.csv")
rem_quality = read_result("rem_quality.csv")
epi_quality = read_result("grd_epi_quality.csv")
grd_summary = read_result("grd_cohort_summary.csv")
cohort = grd_summary.query("era == '2021-2024' and definition == 'TEA_operacional'").iloc[0]

# The opening figures name every source the report reads, not only the two health ones.
education = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "docs" / "study" / "data" / "education_summary_year.csv")
surveys = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "docs" / "study" / "data" / "survey_estimates_verified.csv")
last_edu = education.sort_values("year").iloc[-1]

kpis([
    (number(grd_sources.records.sum()), "Hospital records read · 2019–2024"),
    (number(epi_quality.records_kept.sum()), "Of them, with an autism code"),
    (number(rem_quality.records.sum()), "Community programme rows · 2017–2024"),
    (number(last_edu.pie_harmonised_n), f"School support enrolments with autism · {int(last_edu.year)}"),
    (str(surveys.survey.nunique()), "Household surveys, the only sampled source"),
    (number(cohort.patients), "Identifiers in the trajectory cohort · 2021–2024"),
])
```

This report describes how autism is recognised in the routine administrative records of Chile's public
health and education systems. It brings together every result the study produced, organised by what the
result is about rather than by when it was computed.

**It reads five kinds of source, and they answer different questions.** Two count health events: the
hospital discharge records and the monthly statistical returns of the public network. One counts
education services: the school integration programme, the special schools and the applications
register. One estimates from a sample rather than counting: the household surveys, the only source here
that says anything about a population. And one supplies the layers the others divide by: the population
projections, insurance coverage and primary-care enrolment. A count of records and a survey estimate are
not the same quantity, and the report never plots them as one series.

**Nothing here is prevalence or incidence.** Every number is a count of hospital episodes, community
programme entries, follow-up stocks or school enrolments, presented with its unit, its denominator and
its coverage. The rise these records show is consistent with greater detection, greater demand and
changes in coding during the period of Law 21.545; it does not demonstrate a change in how often autism
occurs.

## What the report contains

**[Methods](methods.qmd).** Sources, case definitions, units, denominators, standardisation, intervals,
trends, spatial analysis, the rules for reading the monthly returns, quality controls, biases and
limitations. It is the common reference for everything that follows.

**[Results](results.qmd).** The principal findings: four panel figures and the nine supplementary
figures that support them, each drawn at render time by the code printed with it.

**[Hospital recognition](hospital.qmd).** The hospital discharge records in depth: magnitude and trend,
age-standardised rates, sex and age, F84 subcategories, the diagnostic position of the code, episode
characteristics, co-diagnoses, readmission, territory and spatial autocorrelation, and the
reconstruction of which diagnoses precede the first observed autism record.

**[Community care](community.qmd).** The monthly statistical returns of the public network: entries to
and discharges from mental-health programmes with an autism code, their population rates, age, sex,
regions, communes and facilities, screening in well-child check-ups, rehabilitation entries, and the
ecological comparison between the two health sources.

**[Education records](education.qmd).** The school integration programme, the special schools and the
applications register: what each one counts, how the strict and harmonised definitions differ, and what
the change of source does to comparability across years.

**[Population surveys](surveys.qmd).** The two household surveys, the only source here that estimates
rather than counts: their domains as the instruments define them, their design-weighted estimates and
the precision of each.

**[Denominators and coverage](denominators.qmd).** The layers every rate divides by — population
projections, insurance coverage, primary-care enrolment — and an independent national discharge
register that counts the same hospital events by principal diagnosis, as a check on the hospital chapter.

**[Result tables](tables.qmd)**, the **extended plates** and **[extended tables](extended_tables.qmd)**
hold the complete material, including the results the main chapters summarise.
**[Reproducibility](reproducibility.qmd)** explains how to rebuild every number in this report.

## Headline results

```{python}
#| label: hallazgos-principales
rates = read_result("grd_rates_national.csv")
trends = read_result("grd_trends_apc.csv")
sex_ratio = read_result("grd_sex_ratio.csv")
rem_rates = read_result("rem_rates_national.csv")
rem_annual = read_result("rem_annual_by_code.csv")
moran = read_result("grd_spatial_moran.csv")

main = rates.loc[(rates.definition == "TEA_operacional") & (rates.role == "cualquiera") & (rates.sex == "TOTAL")]
records = main.loc[main.unit == "records"].set_index("year")
persons = main.loc[main.unit == "persons"].set_index("year")
last_year = int(records.index.max())
apc = trends.query("definition == 'TEA_operacional' and unit == 'records' and role == 'cualquiera' "
                   "and sex == 'TOTAL' and period == '2021-2024'").iloc[0]
ratio = sex_ratio.query("definition == 'TEA_operacional' and unit == 'records' and role == 'cualquiera'").set_index("year")
rem_last = rem_rates.loc[(rem_rates.series == "05990022") & (rem_rates.sex == "TOTAL")].set_index("year")
rem_ingresos = rem_annual.loc[rem_annual.code == "05990022"].set_index("year").Col01
moran_main = moran.query("unit == 'records' and variable == 'sir_eb'").iloc[0]

kpis([
    (number(records.loc[last_year, "asr"], 1), f"Hospitalisations with an autism code per 100 000 person-years, age-standardised · {last_year} (was {number(records.asr.iloc[0], 1)} in {int(records.index.min())})"),
    (number(persons.loc[last_year, "asr"], 1), f"Hospitalised persons with an autism code per 100 000 population · {last_year}"),
    (number(apc.apc, 1) + "%", f"Average annual percent change · 2021–2024 (95% CI: {ci(apc.apc_lo, apc.apc_hi)})"),
    (number(ratio.loc[last_year, "asr_ratio"], 2), f"Male:female rate ratio · {last_year} (was {number(ratio.asr_ratio.iloc[0], 2)} in {int(ratio.index.min())})"),
    (number(rem_last.loc[last_year, "asr"], 1), f"Programme entries with an autism code per 100 000 population, age-standardised · {last_year} ({number(rem_ingresos.loc[last_year])} entries)"),
    (number(moran_main.moran_i, 2), "Moran's I of the smoothed commune hospitalisation ratio (permutation p " + number(moran_main.p_sim, 3) + ")"),
    (number(share(cohort.prior_hospitalization, cohort.patients), 1) + "%", "2021–2024 cohort with observable prior hospitalisations"),
])
```

Hospitalisations and community programme entries with an autism code have grown rapidly since 2021,
more in females than in males, with the greatest intensity between 5 and 14 years of age and with
strong territorial heterogeneity. In the 2021–2024 hospital trajectories, the first autism record almost
always occurs with the code in a secondary position, and only a minority has observable prior
hospitalisations. Those earlier codes do not show that they were ruled out as differential diagnoses:
they may be comorbidities, symptoms or independent reasons for admission.

## How this report was built

Every table and figure is recalculated when the report is rendered; none is pasted in. The chapters read
the aggregated tables in `output_files/consolidacion/` and `docs/study/data/`, both versioned in git, so
the whole report can be rebuilt from a clone without the source microdata. The extraction from the
original microdata runs separately, through the scripts documented in
[Reproducibility](reproducibility.qmd).

The study itself was written over several rounds of revision, which added results without ever changing
one that had already been computed — a claim checked rather than asserted, by hashing every result table
of every round and comparing them pairwise. This report presents the union of all of them as a single
body of work. Where a result comes from a different observation window or an earlier case definition,
the table says so on the spot.

```{python}
#| label: tabla-organizacion
organisation = pd.DataFrame([
    ("Hospital · universe", "Records read, F84 records kept, duplicates, exclusions and coding depth", "grd_epi_quality, grd_annual_positions"),
    ("Hospital · time", "Annual trend, crude and standardised rates, average annual percent change, seasonality", "grd_rates_national, grd_trends_apc, grd_epi_monthly"),
    ("Hospital · person", "Sex ratio, single year of age, age-specific rates", "grd_sex_ratio, grd_epi_age_single, grd_rates_age_specific"),
    ("Hospital · code", "F84 subcategories and diagnostic position", "grd_rates_subcodes, grd_epi_subcodes"),
    ("Hospital · episode", "Admission, activity, specialty, insurance, discharge, length of stay, severity, hospitals", "grd_epi_features, grd_epi_los_*, grd_epi_grd_weight"),
    ("Hospital · burden", "Readmission, multiplicity, co-diagnoses and principal diagnosis", "grd_epi_readmissions, grd_epi_multiplicity, grd_epi_codiagnoses"),
    ("Hospital · place", "Regions, communes, indirect standardisation, Moran and LISA", "grd_rates_regional, grd_rates_comunal, grd_spatial_*"),
    ("Hospital · trajectories", "Identifier continuity, first record, prior diagnoses, sequences, transitions", "grd_cohort_*, grd_first_*, grd_previous_*, grd_sequences"),
    ("Community", "Entries, rates, age and sex, subcategories, regions, communes, facility panel, screening, rehabilitation", "rem_*"),
    ("Results", "Panel figures and supplementary figures, drawn from the published tables", "docs/study/data/*.csv"),
], columns=["Section", "Content", "Inputs"])
show_table(organisation, "The report's sections and the tables that feed them")
```
